268	    return False
269	
270	def _unit_calls(node: ast.AST, sibling_names: set[str], own_name: str) -> set[str]:
271	    calls = set()
272	    for child in ast.walk(node):
273	        if isinstance(child, ast.Name):
274	            if child.id in sibling_names and child.id != own_name:
275	                calls.add(child.id)
276	    return calls
277	
278	def _is_test_function(name: str) -> bool:
279	    """A module-level pytest test function (collected by the ``test_`` prefix).
280	
281	    Embedded pytest tests are not reconstructible code: rebuilding them blind
282	    wastes reconstruction attempts and would clobber the in-module pin. They are
283	    preserved verbatim in the skeleton instead of being harvested as units.
284	    """
285	    raise NotImplementedError
286	
287	def _is_pytest_class(name: str, method_defs: list) -> bool:
288	    """A ``Test``-prefixed class holding ``test*`` methods (a pytest test class).
289	
290	    Distinguishes an embedded pytest class (skip entirely) from a real domain
291	    class that merely starts with ``Test`` (e.g. ``TestAuthorError(Exception)``,
292	    which has no ``test*`` methods).
293	    """
294	    if not name.startswith('Test'):
295	        return False
296	    return any((m.name.startswith('test') for m in method_defs))

298	def harvest_module(module_rel: str, source: str, *, include_methods: bool=False, external_modules: set[str] | frozenset[str] | None=None) -> list[Unit]:
299	    """Parse ``source`` and return its reconstructible function units.
300	
301	    Top-level ``def`` / ``async def`` are always returned (``cls=None``). When
302	    ``include_methods`` is set, each class's methods are also returned as units
303	    with ``qualname`` ``module:Class.method`` and ``cls`` set -- so harvest
304	    handles ClassDef method units, not just module-level functions. Order is
305	    source order (classes contribute their methods at the class's position).
306	
307	    When ``external_modules`` (the set of the project's external 3rd-party
308	    top-level import names) is given AND this module references any of them, the
309	    merged==original ORACLE is unavailable for the whole module: the oracle
310	    execs the ORIGINAL module source in the parent python, which would
311	    ``ImportError`` on the absent dependency. So EVERY unit of a dep-importing
312	    module is flagged ``needs_deps`` and routed (in
313	    :func:`harness.rebuild.task.build_unit_task`) to the oracle-skip +
314	    fuzzer-bypass + venv-scoped-tests path, mirroring the ``impure`` precedent.
315	    """

319	    module_needs_deps = module_has_top_level_external_import(source, external_modules)
320	    units: list[Unit] = []
321	
322	    def _make_unit(node: ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef, cls: str | None) -> Unit:

327	        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
328	            if _is_test_function(node.name):

330	            units.append(_make_unit(node, None))
331	        elif isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) and include_methods:
332	            method_defs = [m for m in node.body if isinstance(m, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef))]

334	                continue
335	            if _class_is_stateful(node):
336	                class_doc = ast.get_docstring(node)
337	                bases = [ast.unparse(base) for base in node.bases]
338	                bases += [f'{kw.arg}={ast.unparse(kw.value)}' for kw in node.keywords]
339	                signature = f'class {node.name}({', '.join(bases)}):' if bases else f'class {node.name}:'

341	                if class_doc is not None:
342	                    skeleton.append(f'    """{class_doc}"""')
343	                for method in method_defs:
344	                    skeleton.append('    ' + _signature_line(method))
345	                    skeleton.append('        raise NotImplementedError')
346	                units.append(Unit(module=module_rel, name=node.name, qualname=f'{module_rel}:{node.name}', signature=signature, docstring=class_doc, decorators=[ast.unparse(dec) for dec in node.decorator_list], cls=node.name, needs_deps=module_needs_deps, rel_import=rel_import, whole_class=True, methods=[method.name for method in method_defs], class_skeleton='\n'.join(skeleton)))

348	                for method in method_defs:
349	                    units.append(_make_unit(method, node.name))
350	    return units
351	
352	def unit_cross_calls(source: str, module_aliases: dict[str, str], importing_rel: str | None=None) -> dict[str, set[tuple[str, str]]]:
353	    """Map each unit's short name -> the cross-module callees it references.
354	
355	    ``module_aliases`` maps an import name (``casing``, ``pkg.sub``) to the rel
356	    path of an intra-project module OTHER than this one. A reference resolves to
357	    a cross-module callee when it is ``<alias>.<attr>`` for an imported module
358	    alias, or a bare name imported via ``from <module> import <name>``. When
359	    ``importing_rel`` (this module's rel path) is given, RELATIVE imports
360	    (``from .x import y`` / ``from . import x``, ``node.level>0``) are resolved
361	    against the importing module's package too (C9.9 packages). The returned value
362	    is ``{unit_name: {(callee_module_rel, callee_name), ...}}``; the loop uses it
363	    to inject cross-module sibling signatures so a caller can be reconstructed
364	    against an already-real callee in another module.
365	    """
366	    raise NotImplementedError
367	
368	def order_units(units: list[Unit]) -> list[Unit]:
369	    """Return units in dependency order (callees before callers).
370	
371	    Pure intra-module: only edges to siblings present in ``units`` count.
372	    Deterministic: ties and cycles fall back to source order, so the result is
373	    stable across runs.
374	    """
375	    by_name: dict[str, Unit] = {}
376	    for unit in units:
377	        by_name.setdefault(unit.name, unit)
378	    source_index = {id(unit): i for i, unit in enumerate(units)}
379	    deps: dict[int, set[int]] = {}
380	    for unit in units:
381	        callees: set[int] = set()
382	        for name in unit.calls:
383	            target = by_name.get(name)
384	            if target is not None and target is not unit:
385	                callees.add(id(target))
386	        deps[id(unit)] = callees
387	    emitted: set[int] = set()
388	    remaining = list(units)
389	    ordered: list[Unit] = []
390	    while remaining:
391	        ready = [u for u in remaining if deps[id(u)] <= emitted]
392	        pool = ready if ready else remaining
393	        nxt = min(pool, key=lambda u: source_index[id(u)])
394	        ordered.append(nxt)
395	        emitted.add(id(nxt))
396	        remaining.remove(nxt)
397	    return ordered
398	'Dependency ordering for harvested intra-module units.'

"""HARVEST: AST-walk a module into reconstructible units + intra-module dep order.

A unit is one top-level ``def`` / ``async def``. For each we capture the
signature line, docstring, decorators, and the set of sibling top-level names
it references (the dependency edges). ``order_units`` returns a dependency
order (callees before callers) so a unit's reconstruction can rely on already
real sibling bodies.

from __future__ import annotations
import ast
from dataclasses import dataclass
from dataclasses import field
from harness.rebuild.deps import external_units
from harness.rebuild.deps import module_has_top_level_external_import

@dataclass
class Unit:
    """One reconstructible function (top-level ``def`` or a class method).

    ``cls`` is ``None`` for a module-level function; for a method it is the
    enclosing class name and ``qualname`` reads ``module:Class.method``.
    """
    module: str
    name: str
    qualname: str
    signature: str
    docstring: str | None
    decorators: list[str]
    calls: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    cls: str | None = None
    impure: bool = False
    needs_deps: bool = False
    untyped: bool = False
    whole_class: bool = False
    methods: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    class_skeleton: str = ''
    rel_import: bool = False
    self_mutating: bool = False
    unfuzzable: bool = False
_IMPURE_MODULES = frozenset({'time', 'random', 'datetime', 'os', 'sys', 'socket', 'secrets', 'uuid', 'subprocess', 'requests', 'urllib', 'shutil', 'tempfile', 'threading', 'multiprocessing', 'asyncio'})

def _module_global_names(tree: ast.Module) -> set[str]:

    A module-level helper like inflection's ``_irregular`` (``PLURALS.insert(...)``,
    returns ``None``) is contractually a side-effecting INITIALIZER -- it is only
    ever called at import time with valid inputs, never the arbitrary fuzz inputs
    the merged==original differential oracle throws at it. Fuzzing it produces
    spurious ``exception_mismatch`` divergences (e.g. ``caps('')`` -> IndexError on
    the original) that no correct reconstruction can match. Worse, such a helper is
    typically CALLED at module level, so until it is reconstructed every other
    unit's candidate module fails to import. Route it (like ``impure``) to the
    tests-only path so the authored pytest oracle -- which calls it with real
    inputs -- is the honest gate. Detection: a rebind of a ``global``-declared
    name, or an in-place subscript/attribute store or mutating method call on a
    module global.

    mutating_methods = frozenset({'append', 'insert', 'extend', 'remove', 'pop', 'clear', 'sort', 'reverse', 'update', 'add', 'discard', 'setdefault', 'popitem', 'intersection_update', 'difference_update', 'symmetric_difference_update'})

        while isinstance(expr, (ast.Attribute, ast.Subscript)):

    def _leaf_targets(targets: list[ast.expr]):

            if isinstance(target, (ast.Tuple, ast.List)):
                stack.extend(target.elts)
            elif isinstance(target, ast.Starred):
                stack.append(target.value)

                yield target

        if isinstance(child, (ast.Assign, ast.AugAssign, ast.AnnAssign)):
            targets = child.targets if isinstance(child, ast.Assign) else [child.target]

                if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
                    if target.id in global_decls:
                        return True
                elif isinstance(target, (ast.Subscript, ast.Attribute)):
                    if _root_name(target) in module_globals:
                        return True

            func = child.func
            if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in mutating_methods:

def _signature_line(node: ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef) -> str:
    """Render the ``def`` header line (no body) for a function node."""
    prefix = 'async def' if isinstance(node, ast.AsyncFunctionDef) else 'def'
    args = ast.unparse(node.args)
    returns = f' -> {ast.unparse(node.returns)}' if node.returns is not None else ''
    return f'{prefix} {node.name}({args}){returns}:'

def _has_relative_import(tree: ast.Module) -> bool:
    """True iff the module uses a relative import (``from .x import y``).

    The merged==original differential oracle execs the module source STANDALONE
    (no package context), so a relative import raises ``ImportError`` there. A
    module that uses one therefore can't be gated by that oracle and must route
    to the tests-only path (run inside the real package), mirroring the ``impure``
    precedent -- a conservative false oracle-skip only costs the redundant oracle.
    """
    return any((isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and (node.level or 0) > 0 for node in ast.walk(tree)))

def _class_is_stateful(node: ast.ClassDef) -> bool:
    """True iff a class shares instance state across methods (reconstruct as ONE).

    Stateful = an ``__init__`` STORES ``self.<attr>`` AND at least one OTHER
    method READS a ``self.<attr>``. Such a class cannot be reconstructed
    per-method: a method verified first FAILS because the shared multi-method
    test also exercises its siblings, which are still ``NotImplementedError``
    stubs (the #34 per-method-recon-needs-per-method-tests gotcha). So it routes
    to CLASS-granular reconstruction (all methods in one blind submission, gated
    by the class's tests). A stateless class keeps per-method recon (#34).

        attrs = set()
        for sub in ast.walk(method):

def _is_self_mutating(node: ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef) -> bool:
    """True iff a method only mutates ``self`` with no meaningful fuzz domain.

    A dataclass ``__post_init__`` (or any method that STORES ``self.<attr>`` and
    returns no value) has no constructible fuzz inputs. The merged==original
    differential ORACLE resolves the target by name in the MODULE namespace, but
    a method lives inside its class, so the lookup finds nothing and reports every
    input as a matching ``NameError`` -> a VACUOUS ``equivalent=True`` (it would
    "pass" a body that is plainly WRONG). Such a unit must route to the tests-only
    path (like ``impure``) so the test-author pytest oracle is the sole, honest
    gate. ``__post_init__`` is always caught; the general rule covers other
    self-mutating, value-less methods (setters, in-place updates).
    """
    if node.name == '__post_init__':
        return True
    stores_self = False
    for sub in ast.walk(node):
        if isinstance(sub, ast.Return) and sub.value is not None:
            return False
        if isinstance(sub, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(sub.ctx, ast.Store) and isinstance(sub.value, ast.Name) and (sub.value.id == 'self'):

_FUZZABLE_NAMES = frozenset({'None', 'NoneType', 'bool', 'int', 'float', 'str', 'bytes', 'Any'})
_FUZZABLE_CONTAINERS = frozenset({'list', 'List', 'set', 'Set', 'tuple', 'Tuple', 'dict', 'Dict', 'Optional', 'Union'})

def _is_fuzzable_annotation(node: ast.expr | None) -> bool:
    """True iff ``node`` is built only from fuzzer-synthesizable primitives/containers."""

        return False
    if isinstance(node, ast.Constant):

    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):

            return False

def _has_unfuzzable_params(node: ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef) -> bool:
    """True iff a value-bearing param is TYPED with a type the fuzzer can't synthesize.

    A ``Path``/domain-object param is fuzzed as a garbage ``int`` (the strategy
    table's fallback), so the merged==original differential ORACLE over-fuzzes a
    correct body into a FALSE divergence (e.g. a thin constructor wrapper that
    forwards path args into a dataclass -- ``target.mathlib_descriptor``). Such a
    unit routes to the tests-only path, where the authored oracle constructs real
    inputs. ``self``/``cls`` are exempt; an UN-typed param is handled by ``untyped``.

    args = node.args
    params = [*args.posonlyargs, *args.args, *args.kwonlyargs]

        params.append(args.vararg)
    if args.kwarg is not None:
        params.append(args.kwarg)

def _has_untyped_params(node: ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef) -> bool:

    A method's leading ``self``/``cls`` is exempt (it is never a fuzz input). A

    differential fuzzer (``diff_fuzzer._strategy_for_annotation``) with an
    unconstrained input domain, which over-fuzzes a correct body into a FALSE
    value-divergence (the #34 ``longest([[]])`` reject), so such a unit must route
    to the tests-only path rather than the merged==original fuzz oracle.
    """
    args = node.args
    params = [*args.posonlyargs, *args.args, *args.kwonlyargs]
    if args.vararg is not None:
        params.append(args.vararg)
    if args.kwarg is not None:
        params.append(args.kwarg)
    for param in params:
        if param.arg in ('self', 'cls'):
            continue
        if param.annotation is None:

    return False

def _unit_calls(node: ast.AST, sibling_names: set[str], own_name: str) -> set[str]:
    calls = set()

    ``ImportError`` on the absent dependency. So EVERY unit of a dep-importing

                    skeleton.append('        raise NotImplementedError')

def unit_cross_calls(source: str, module_aliases: dict[str, str], importing_rel: str | None=None) -> dict[str, set[tuple[str, str]]]:
    """Map each unit's short name -> the cross-module callees it references.

    ``module_aliases`` maps an import name (``casing``, ``pkg.sub``) to the rel
    path of an intra-project module OTHER than this one. A reference resolves to
    a cross-module callee when it is ``<alias>.<attr>`` for an imported module
    alias, or a bare name imported via ``from <module> import <name>``. When
    ``importing_rel`` (this module's rel path) is given, RELATIVE imports
    (``from .x import y`` / ``from . import x``, ``node.level>0``) are resolved
    against the importing module's package too (C9.9 packages). The returned value
    is ``{unit_name: {(callee_module_rel, callee_name), ...}}``; the loop uses it
    to inject cross-module sibling signatures so a caller can be reconstructed
    against an already-real callee in another module.

    raise NotImplementedError

def order_units(units: list[Unit]) -> list[Unit]:
    """Return units in dependency order (callees before callers).

    Pure intra-module: only edges to siblings present in ``units`` count.
    Deterministic: ties and cycles fall back to source order, so the result is
    stable across runs.
    """
    by_name: dict[str, Unit] = {}
    for unit in units:
        by_name.setdefault(unit.name, unit)
    source_index = {id(unit): i for i, unit in enumerate(units)}
    deps: dict[int, set[int]] = {}
    for unit in units:
        callees: set[int] = set()
        for name in unit.calls:
            target = by_name.get(name)
            if target is not None and target is not unit:
                callees.add(id(target))
        deps[id(unit)] = callees
    emitted: set[int] = set()
    remaining = list(units)
    ordered: list[Unit] = []
    while remaining:
        ready = [u for u in remaining if deps[id(u)] <= emitted]
        pool = ready if ready else remaining
        nxt = min(pool, key=lambda u: source_index[id(u)])
        ordered.append(nxt)
        emitted.add(id(nxt))
        remaining.remove(nxt)
    return ordered

7	real sibling bodies.

12	from dataclasses import field

14	from harness.rebuild.deps import module_has_top_level_external_import

19	
20	    ``cls`` is ``None`` for a module-level function; for a method it is the
21	    enclosing class name and ``qualname`` reads ``module:Class.method``.
22	    """

24	    name: str
25	    qualname: str
26	    signature: str
27	    docstring: str | None
28	    decorators: list[str]
29	    calls: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
30	    cls: str | None = None
31	    impure: bool = False

    value-divergence (the #34 ``longest([[]])`` reject), so such a unit must route
    to the tests-only path rather than the merged==original fuzz oracle.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def _unit_calls(node: ast.AST, sibling_names: set[str], own_name: str) -> set[str]:
    calls = set()
    for child in ast.walk(node):
        if isinstance(child, ast.Name):
            if child.id in sibling_names and child.id != own_name:
                calls.add(child.id)
    return calls

def _is_test_function(name: str) -> bool:
    """A module-level pytest test function (collected by the ``test_`` prefix).

    Embedded pytest tests are not reconstructible code: rebuilding them blind
    wastes reconstruction attempts and would clobber the in-module pin. They are
    preserved verbatim in the skeleton instead of being harvested as units.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def _is_pytest_class(name: str, method_defs: list) -> bool:
    """A ``Test``-prefixed class holding ``test*`` methods (a pytest test class).

    Distinguishes an embedded pytest class (skip entirely) from a real domain
    class that merely starts with ``Test`` (e.g. ``TestAuthorError(Exception)``,
    which has no ``test*`` methods).
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def harvest_module(module_rel: str, source: str, *, include_methods: bool=False, external_modules: set[str] | frozenset[str] | None=None) -> list[Unit]:
    """Parse ``source`` and return its reconstructible function units.

    Top-level ``def`` / ``async def`` are always returned (``cls=None``). When
    ``include_methods`` is set, each class's methods are also returned as units
    with ``qualname`` ``module:Class.method`` and ``cls`` set -- so harvest
    handles ClassDef method units, not just module-level functions. Order is
    source order (classes contribute their methods at the class's position).

    When ``external_modules`` (the set of the project's external 3rd-party
    top-level import names) is given AND this module references any of them, the
    merged==original ORACLE is unavailable for the whole module: the oracle
    execs the ORIGINAL module source in the parent python, which would
    ``ImportError`` on the absent dependency. So EVERY unit of a dep-importing
    module is flagged ``needs_deps`` and routed (in
    :func:`harness.rebuild.task.build_unit_task`) to the oracle-skip +
    fuzzer-bypass + venv-scoped-tests path, mirroring the ``impure`` precedent.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def unit_cross_calls(source: str, module_aliases: dict[str, str], importing_rel: str | None=None) -> dict[str, set[tuple[str, str]]]:
    """Map each unit's short name -> the cross-module callees it references.

    ``module_aliases`` maps an import name (``casing``, ``pkg.sub``) to the rel
    path of an intra-project module OTHER than this one. A reference resolves to
    a cross-module callee when it is ``<alias>.<attr>`` for an imported module
    alias, or a bare name imported via ``from <module> import <name>``. When
    ``importing_rel`` (this module's rel path) is given, RELATIVE imports
    (``from .x import y`` / ``from . import x``, ``node.level>0``) are resolved
    against the importing module's package too (C9.9 packages). The returned value
    is ``{unit_name: {(callee_module_rel, callee_name), ...}}``; the loop uses it
    to inject cross-module sibling signatures so a caller can be reconstructed
    against an already-real callee in another module.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def order_units(units: list[Unit]) -> list[Unit]:
    """Return units in dependency order (callees before callers).

    Pure intra-module: only edges to siblings present in ``units`` count.
    Deterministic: ties and cycles fall back to source order, so the result is
    stable across runs.
    """
    by_name: dict[str, Unit] = {}
    for unit in units:
        by_name.setdefault(unit.name, unit)
    source_index = {id(unit): i for i, unit in enumerate(units)}
    deps: dict[int, set[int]] = {}
    for unit in units:
        callees: set[int] = set()
        for name in unit.calls:
            target = by_name.get(name)
            if target is not None and target is not unit:
                callees.add(id(target))
        deps[id(unit)] = callees
    emitted: set[int] = set()
    remaining = list(units)
    ordered: list[Unit] = []
    while remaining:
        ready = [u for u in remaining if deps[id(u)] <= emitted]
        pool = ready if ready else remaining
        nxt = min(pool, key=lambda u: source_index[id(u)])
        ordered.append(nxt)
        emitted.add(id(nxt))
        remaining.remove(nxt)
    return ordered

1	"""DEPS: discover a project's EXTERNAL dependencies + the units that use them.
2	
3	The clean-room rebuild engine needs to reconstruct a project in an
4	environment-faithful way: a unit that imports a 3rd-party package can't be
5	rebuilt BLIND against the merged==original oracle (the dep is unavailable /
6	nondeterministic), so it must be routed to the oracle-skip + fuzzer-bypass
7	path. Two responsibilities live here:
8	
9	  * :func:`discover_dependencies` -- extract the project's declared external
10	    deps (and the manifest files they came from), trying requirements files,
11	    ``pyproject.toml``, ``setup.cfg``, ``setup.py`` in that order, with a
12	    last-resort AST import scan. The FIRST source that yields a dependency
13	    wins; sources are never merged.
14	  * :func:`external_units` -- given one module's source and the set of known
15	    external top-level package names, return the names of the functions /
16	    methods whose body references a name bound from one of those deps.
17	
18	Pure stdlib only (``ast`` / ``re`` / ``sys`` / ``configparser`` / ``tomllib``
19	/ ``pathlib``); no filesystem access outside ``source_root`` and no
20	home-directory lookups (clone-portable).
21	"""
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	import ast
24	import configparser
25	import re
26	import sys
27	import tomllib
28	from pathlib import Path
29	_SKIP_DIRS = {'__pycache__', '.git', '.hg', 'state', 'build', 'dist', '.eggs', 'node_modules', '.tox', '.venv', 'venv', '.mypy_cache', '.pytest_cache'}
30	
31	def _norm_name(dep: str) -> str:
32	    """PEP 503 normalized project name of a requirement string (or '').
33	
34	    Reads the leading name token (stopping at the first version operator,
35	    extras bracket, marker, or URL ``@``), then lowercases and collapses every
36	    run of ``-`` / ``_`` / ``.`` to a single ``-``.
37	    """
38	    match = re.match('\\s*([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)', dep)
39	    if not match:
40	        return ''
41	    return re.sub('[-_.]+', '-', match.group(1)).lower()
42	
43	def _dedup(deps: list[str]) -> list[str]:
44	    """De-duplicate by PEP 503 normalized name, preserving the first-seen line."""
45	    seen: set[str] = set()
46	    result: list[str] = []
47	    for dep in deps:
48	        name = _norm_name(dep)
49	        if not name or name in seen:
50	            continue
51	        seen.add(name)
52	        result.append(dep)
53	    return result
54	
55	def _include_target(line: str) -> str | None:
56	    """Return the FILE of a ``-r FILE`` / ``--requirement FILE`` line, else None."""
57	    match = re.match('\\s*(?:-r|--requirement)(?:\\s+|\\s*=\\s*)(.+)', line)
58	    if not match:
59	        return None
60	    return match.group(1).strip().strip('\'"') or None
61	
62	def _from_requirements(root: Path) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
63	    """Parse ``requirements*.txt`` / ``requirements.lock`` at ``root``.
64	
65	    Returns ``(deps, requirements_files)``. Comment lines and inline comments
66	    are stripped, blank lines dropped, ``-`` option lines skipped EXCEPT
67	    ``-r``/``--requirement`` includes (followed recursively, relative to
68	    ``root``). Each manifest actually read is recorded as a rel POSIX path.
69	    """
70	    deps: list[str] = []
71	    files: list[str] = []
72	    seen: set[Path] = set()
73	
74	    def _read(path: Path) -> None:
75	        resolved = path.resolve()
76	        if resolved in seen or not path.is_file():
77	            return
78	        seen.add(resolved)
79	        files.append(path.relative_to(root).as_posix())
80	        for raw in path.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').splitlines():
81	            line = raw.strip()
82	            if not line or line.startswith('#'):
83	                continue
84	            line = re.split('\\s+#', line, maxsplit=1)[0].strip()
85	            if not line:
86	                continue
87	            if line.startswith('-'):
88	                target = _include_target(line)
89	                if target is not None:
90	                    _read(root / target)
91	                continue
92	            deps.append(line)
93	    manifests = sorted(root.glob('requirements*.txt'))
94	    lock = root / 'requirements.lock'
95	    if lock.is_file():
96	        manifests.append(lock)
97	    for manifest in manifests:
98	        _read(manifest)
99	    return (deps, files)
100	
101	def _from_pyproject(root: Path) -> list[str]:
102	    """``[project].dependencies`` + ``[tool.poetry.dependencies]`` keys (no 'python')."""
103	    path = root / 'pyproject.toml'
104	    if not path.is_file():
105	        return []
106	    try:
107	        data = tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'))
108	    except (tomllib.TOMLDecodeError, OSError):
109	        return []
110	    deps: list[str] = []
111	    project = data.get('project')
112	    if isinstance(project, dict):
113	        for dep in project.get('dependencies') or []:
114	            if isinstance(dep, str):
115	                deps.append(dep)
116	    tool = data.get('tool')
117	    if isinstance(tool, dict):
118	        poetry = tool.get('poetry')
119	        if isinstance(poetry, dict):
120	            poetry_deps = poetry.get('dependencies')
121	            if isinstance(poetry_deps, dict):
122	                deps.extend((name for name in poetry_deps if name != 'python'))
123	    return deps
124	
125	def _from_setup_cfg(root: Path) -> list[str]:
126	    """``[options] install_requires`` (one dependency per line)."""
127	    path = root / 'setup.cfg'
128	    if not path.is_file():
129	        return []
130	    parser = configparser.ConfigParser()
131	    try:
132	        parser.read(path, encoding='utf-8')
133	    except (configparser.Error, OSError):
134	        return []
135	    raw = parser.get('options', 'install_requires', fallback='')
136	    deps: list[str] = []
137	    for line in raw.splitlines():
138	        dep = line.strip()
139	        if dep:
140	            deps.append(dep)
141	    return deps
142	
143	def _from_setup_py(root: Path) -> list[str]:
144	    """Best-effort: a literal ``install_requires=[...]`` string list (AST)."""
145	    path = root / 'setup.py'
146	    if not path.is_file():
147	        return []
148	    try:
149	        tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'))
150	    except (SyntaxError, ValueError, OSError):
151	        return []
152	    for node in ast.walk(tree):
153	        if isinstance(node, ast.keyword) and node.arg == 'install_requires' and isinstance(node.value, ast.List):
154	            deps: list[str] = []
155	            for elt in node.value.elts:
156	                if isinstance(elt, ast.Constant) and isinstance(elt.value, str):
157	                    deps.append(elt.value)
158	            return deps
159	    return []
160	
161	def _project_py_files(root: Path) -> list[Path]:
162	    """Rel paths of the project's own ``.py`` files (skipping vendor/build dirs)."""
163	    result: list[Path] = []
164	    for path in sorted(root.rglob('*.py')):
165	        rel = path.relative_to(root)
166	        if any((part in _SKIP_DIRS for part in rel.parts)):
167	            continue
168	        result.append(rel)
169	    return result
170	
171	def _intra_project_names(root: Path, py_files: list[Path]) -> set[str]:
172	    """Top-level package/module names owned by the project (+ ``source_root.name``)."""
173	    names: set[str] = {root.name}
174	    for rel in py_files:
175	        parts = rel.parts
176	        if not parts:
177	            continue
178	        if len(parts) == 1:
179	            names.add(rel.stem)
180	        else:
181	            names.add(parts[0])
182	    return names
183	
184	def _from_ast(root: Path) -> list[str]:
185	    """Fallback: external top-level import names across the project's modules.
186	
187	    Top-level (module-body) imports across every project ``.py`` file, minus
188	    the stdlib (``sys.stdlib_module_names``) and the project's own top-level
189	    package/module names. Relative imports are intra-project and ignored.
190	    """
191	    py_files = _project_py_files(root)
192	    intra = _intra_project_names(root, py_files)
193	    stdlib = set(sys.stdlib_module_names)
194	    found: set[str] = set()
195	    for rel in py_files:
196	        path = root / rel
197	        try:
198	            tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'))
199	        except (SyntaxError, ValueError, OSError):
200	            continue
201	        for node in tree.body:
202	            if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
203	                for alias in node.names:
204	                    found.add(alias.name.split('.')[0])
205	            elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
206	                if node.level:
207	                    continue
208	                if node.module:
209	                    found.add(node.module.split('.')[0])
210	    external = found - stdlib - intra
211	    return sorted(external)

213	def discover_dependencies(source_root) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
214	    """Discover ``(dependencies, requirements_files)`` for ``source_root``.
215	
216	    Dependency sources are tried in order -- requirements manifests,
217	    ``pyproject.toml``, ``setup.cfg``, ``setup.py``, then an AST import scan --
218	    and the FIRST that yields any dependency wins (sources are not merged).
219	    Dependencies are de-duplicated by PEP 503 normalized name (the first-seen
220	    line, with its version specifier, is kept). ``requirements_files`` always
221	    lists every requirements manifest found as a rel POSIX path, regardless of
222	    which source supplied the dependencies.
223	    """
224	    root = Path(source_root)
225	    deps, requirements_files = _from_requirements(root)
226	    if not deps:
227	        deps = _from_pyproject(root)
228	    if not deps:
229	        deps = _from_setup_cfg(root)
230	    if not deps:
231	        deps = _from_setup_py(root)
232	    if not deps:
233	        deps = _from_ast(root)
234	    return (_dedup(deps), requirements_files)

236	def _references(node: ast.AST, names: set[str]) -> bool:
237	    """True iff ``node``'s subtree references any name in ``names``.
238	
239	    A bare ``ast.Name`` use counts; an attribute access ``pkg.attr`` is caught
240	    via the ``ast.Name`` at the root of the attribute chain, which ``ast.walk``
241	    visits directly.
242	    """
243	    return any((isinstance(sub, ast.Name) and sub.id in names for sub in ast.walk(node)))

245	def external_units(module_source: str, external_modules) -> set[str]:
246	    """Names of top-level functions/methods that depend on an external package.
247	
248	    A unit (top-level ``def``/``async def`` or class method) is included when
249	    EITHER:

251	    (a) it references a name bound by a MODULE-TOP-LEVEL import of an external
252	        module -- ``import pkg`` binds ``pkg`` (or its asname); ``from pkg
253	        import a, b as c`` binds ``a`` and ``c`` -- detected via the preserved
254	        ``_references`` helper, OR
255	    (b) its OWN body contains a FUNCTION-LOCAL import of an external module
256	        (e.g. ``def f(): import inflection`` or ``def f(): from inflection
257	        import pluralize``).

259	    ``external_modules`` is the set of known external top-level package names
260	    (e.g. ``{'inflection'}``). Returns an empty set when ``external_modules``
261	    is falsy or the source is unparseable. Names are returned as their short
262	    name (``node.name``).
263	    """
264	    if not external_modules:
265	        return set()
266	    try:
267	        tree = ast.parse(module_source)
268	    except (SyntaxError, ValueError):
269	        return set()
270	    bound: set[str] = set()
271	    for node in tree.body:
272	        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
273	            for alias in node.names:
274	                if alias.name.split('.')[0] in external_modules:
275	                    bound.add(alias.asname or alias.name.split('.')[0])
276	        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
277	            if node.level:
278	                continue
279	            if node.module and node.module.split('.')[0] in external_modules:
280	                for alias in node.names:
281	                    bound.add(alias.asname or alias.name)

284	        for sub in ast.walk(unit):
285	            if isinstance(sub, ast.Import):
286	                if any((alias.name.split('.')[0] in external_modules for alias in sub.names)):
287	                    return True
288	            elif isinstance(sub, ast.ImportFrom):
289	                if sub.level:

1	"""DISCOVER: build a TargetDescriptor from a BARE project directory.
2	
3	Session #31's engine required a hand-authored descriptor (explicit module list,
4	test list, selector). This makes the engine work on an ARBITRARY python/ast
5	project -- including JanusMask itself -- by scanning a directory: classify each
6	``.py`` file as a rebuild target module, a pytest spec file, or seed scaffolding
7	(package ``__init__`` / ``conftest``), then synthesize the descriptor fields the
8	loop needs (full test command + per-unit ``-k`` selector).
9	
10	Callers may still override any inferred field (``modules=`` / ``test_files=`` /
11	``seed_files=``) to rebuild a narrow SLICE of a large project without scanning
12	the whole tree (e.g. a single JanusMask leaf module into JR).
13	"""
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	import ast
16	from pathlib import Path
17	from harness.rebuild.deps import discover_dependencies
18	from harness.rebuild.target import TargetDescriptor
19	__all__ = ['discover_modules', 'build_descriptor', 'discover_dependencies', 'module_import_graph', 'order_modules', 'relative_base']
20	_SEED_NAMES = {'__init__.py', 'conftest.py'}
21	_SKIP_DIRS = {'__pycache__', '.git', '.hg', 'state', 'build', 'dist', '.eggs', 'node_modules'}
22	
23	def _is_test_file(name: str) -> bool:
24	    raise NotImplementedError
25

27	    raise NotImplementedError
28	
29	def discover_modules(source_root: Path) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[str]]:
30	    """Scan ``source_root`` and return ``(modules, test_files, seed_files)``.
31	
32	    Paths are returned relative to ``source_root``, POSIX-style, sorted. Test
33	    files (``test_*.py`` / ``*_test.py``) and seeds (``__init__.py`` /
34	    ``conftest.py``) are NOT rebuild targets; everything else is a module.
35	    Hidden dirs, ``__pycache__``, ``state``, and build artifacts are skipped.
36	    """
37	    raise NotImplementedError
38	
39	def _stem_map(modules: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
40	    """Map an import name -> module rel path for intra-project resolution.
41	
42	    A flat module ``casing.py`` is importable as ``casing``; a packaged module
43	    ``pkg/sub.py`` as ``pkg.sub`` (and, best-effort, its leaf ``sub``). Both the
44	    dotted path and the leaf are registered so ``import casing`` and
45	    ``from pkg.sub import x`` both resolve.
46	    """
47	    raise NotImplementedError
48	
49	def relative_base(importing_rel: str, level: int) -> list[str] | None:

"""DISCOVER: build a TargetDescriptor from a BARE project directory.

Session #31's engine required a hand-authored descriptor (explicit module list,
test list, selector). This makes the engine work on an ARBITRARY python/ast
project -- including JanusMask itself -- by scanning a directory: classify each
``.py`` file as a rebuild target module, a pytest spec file, or seed scaffolding
(package ``__init__`` / ``conftest``), then synthesize the descriptor fields the
loop needs (full test command + per-unit ``-k`` selector).

Callers may still override any inferred field (``modules=`` / ``test_files=`` /
``seed_files=``) to rebuild a narrow SLICE of a large project without scanning
the whole tree (e.g. a single JanusMask leaf module into JR).
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import ast
from pathlib import Path
from harness.rebuild.deps import discover_dependencies
from harness.rebuild.target import TargetDescriptor
__all__ = ['discover_modules', 'build_descriptor', 'discover_dependencies', 'module_import_graph', 'order_modules', 'relative_base']
_SEED_NAMES = {'__init__.py', 'conftest.py'}
_SKIP_DIRS = {'__pycache__', '.git', '.hg', 'state', 'build', 'dist', '.eggs', 'node_modules'}

def _is_test_file(name: str) -> bool:
    raise NotImplementedError

def _skip_dir(rel_parts: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
    raise NotImplementedError

def discover_modules(source_root: Path) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[str]]:
    """Scan ``source_root`` and return ``(modules, test_files, seed_files)``.

    Paths are returned relative to ``source_root``, POSIX-style, sorted. Test
    files (``test_*.py`` / ``*_test.py``) and seeds (``__init__.py`` /
    ``conftest.py``) are NOT rebuild targets; everything else is a module.
    Hidden dirs, ``__pycache__``, ``state``, and build artifacts are skipped.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def _stem_map(modules: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Map an import name -> module rel path for intra-project resolution.

    A flat module ``casing.py`` is importable as ``casing``; a packaged module
    ``pkg/sub.py`` as ``pkg.sub`` (and, best-effort, its leaf ``sub``). Both the
    dotted path and the leaf are registered so ``import casing`` and
    ``from pkg.sub import x`` both resolve.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def relative_base(importing_rel: str, level: int) -> list[str] | None:
    """Return the absolute dotted prefix a relative import resolves against.

    For a module ``pkg/sub.py`` (dotted ``pkg.sub``, package ``pkg``) a
    ``level``-dot relative import drops ``level-1`` trailing components from the
    importing module's PACKAGE (Python's ``importlib`` semantics): ``level=1`` ->
    ``['pkg']`` (current package), ``level=2`` -> ``[]`` (parent / top-level).
    Returns ``None`` when the level ascends beyond the top-level package (an
    invalid relative import). Callers append the imported module/name to build the
    absolute dotted target, then resolve it via :func:`_stem_map`.
    """
    package_parts = importing_rel.split('/')[:-1]
    cut = len(package_parts) - (level - 1)
    if cut < 0:
        return None
    return package_parts[:cut]

def _import_from_targets(importing_rel: str, node: ast.ImportFrom) -> list[str]:
    """Absolute dotted module name(s) an ``ImportFrom`` (absolute OR relative) names.

    Absolute ``from pkg.x import y`` -> ``['pkg.x']``. Relative ``from .x import y``
    / ``from . import x`` are resolved through :func:`relative_base` to the
    absolute package, then each ``from . import <name>`` submodule (or the single
    ``from .x`` module) is returned. Empty when a relative import is out of bounds.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def module_import_graph(source_root: Path, modules: list[str]) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
    """Return ``{module_rel: set(intra-project module_rels it imports)}``.

    Only edges to OTHER modules in ``modules`` count (external deps and stdlib
    are ignored). Both top-level and function-local imports are considered, so a
    lazily-imported cross-module dependency still orders/taints correctly. A
    module never depends on itself.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def order_modules(source_root: Path, modules: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Order ``modules`` so an imported (callee) module precedes its importer.

    Deterministic depth-first topological order over
    :func:`module_import_graph`; ties and import CYCLES fall back to the given
    source order (so a circular ``a <-> b`` import pair is stable, never an
    error). Unit-level call dependencies are resolved separately by the loop, so
    a module-level cycle does not block reconstruction.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def build_descriptor(source_root: Path, *, output_dir: Path, stash_dir: Path, name: str | None=None, modules: list[str] | None=None, test_files: list[str] | None=None, seed_files: list[str] | None=None, dependencies: list[str] | None=None, requirements_files: list[str] | None=None) -> TargetDescriptor:
    """Build a working ``TargetDescriptor`` from a bare dir (fields auto-inferred).

    Any of ``modules`` / ``test_files`` / ``seed_files`` may be supplied to
    rebuild a narrow slice; whatever is omitted is discovered by scanning.
    ``unit_test_selector`` is derived only when exactly one test file exists
    (the unambiguous case); otherwise it is left empty and the loop falls back
    to running the whole test list per unit. External ``dependencies`` and the
    ``requirements_files`` they came from are discovered via
    :func:`harness.rebuild.deps.discover_dependencies` unless supplied (so the
    replicant can provision its own ``.venv`` and run standalone).
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

"""Per-``meta_task_type`` narrow-fuzz harness (W77b).

Runs property-style fuzzing on bypass-eligible canaries that the
diff-fuzzer cannot exercise (validators that take ``ast.AST`` inputs,
hook callbacks, internal plumbing). Per-type modules register under
``harness/narrow_fuzz/<meta_task_type>.py`` and expose one public
function::

    def fuzz(module_name: str, module_src: str, *, timeout: float = 5.0) -> str | None

Returns ``None`` on pass/skip; descriptive error string on fail. The
public :func:`run_narrow_fuzz` dispatches via :data:`._registry.REGISTRY`;
unregistered types return ``None`` silently to preserve bypass semantics
per the brief's G3 ("a type without a narrow-fuzz module still
bypasses").
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from harness.narrow_fuzz._registry import REGISTRY


def run_narrow_fuzz(
    meta_task_type: str,
    module_name: str,
    module_src: str,
    *,
    timeout: float = 5.0,
) -> str | None:
    """Dispatch to the per-type fuzz module.

    Returns ``None`` when no module is registered for
    ``meta_task_type`` (skip; preserves bypass semantics).
    """
    fuzz_fn = REGISTRY.get(meta_task_type)
    if fuzz_fn is None:
        return None
    return fuzz_fn(module_name, module_src, timeout=timeout)


__all__ = ["run_narrow_fuzz"]

def _skip_dir(rel_parts: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
    raise NotImplementedError

def discover_modules(source_root: Path) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[str]]:
    """Scan ``source_root`` and return ``(modules, test_files, seed_files)``.

    Paths are returned relative to ``source_root``, POSIX-style, sorted. Test
    files (``test_*.py`` / ``*_test.py``) and seeds (``__init__.py`` /
    ``conftest.py``) are NOT rebuild targets; everything else is a module.
    Hidden dirs, ``__pycache__``, ``state``, and build artifacts are skipped.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def _stem_map(modules: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Map an import name -> module rel path for intra-project resolution.

    A flat module ``casing.py`` is importable as ``casing``; a packaged module
    ``pkg/sub.py`` as ``pkg.sub`` (and, best-effort, its leaf ``sub``). Both the
    dotted path and the leaf are registered so ``import casing`` and
    ``from pkg.sub import x`` both resolve.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def relative_base(importing_rel: str, level: int) -> list[str] | None:
    """Return the absolute dotted prefix a relative import resolves against.

    For a module ``pkg/sub.py`` (dotted ``pkg.sub``, package ``pkg``) a
    ``level``-dot relative import drops ``level-1`` trailing components from the
    importing module's PACKAGE (Python's ``importlib`` semantics): ``level=1`` ->
    ``['pkg']`` (current package), ``level=2`` -> ``[]`` (parent / top-level).
    Returns ``None`` when the level ascends beyond the top-level package (an
    invalid relative import). Callers append the imported module/name to build the
    absolute dotted target, then resolve it via :func:`_stem_map`.
    """
    package_parts = importing_rel.split('/')[:-1]
    cut = len(package_parts) - (level - 1)
    if cut < 0:
        return None
    return package_parts[:cut]

def _import_from_targets(importing_rel: str, node: ast.ImportFrom) -> list[str]:
    """Absolute dotted module name(s) an ``ImportFrom`` (absolute OR relative) names.

    Absolute ``from pkg.x import y`` -> ``['pkg.x']``. Relative ``from .x import y``
    / ``from . import x`` are resolved through :func:`relative_base` to the
    absolute package, then each ``from . import <name>`` submodule (or the single
    ``from .x`` module) is returned. Empty when a relative import is out of bounds.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def module_import_graph(source_root: Path, modules: list[str]) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
    """Return ``{module_rel: set(intra-project module_rels it imports)}``.

    Only edges to OTHER modules in ``modules`` count (external deps and stdlib
    are ignored). Both top-level and function-local imports are considered, so a
    lazily-imported cross-module dependency still orders/taints correctly. A
    module never depends on itself.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

"""DISCOVER: build a TargetDescriptor from a BARE project directory.

Session #31's engine required a hand-authored descriptor (explicit module list,
test list, selector). This makes the engine work on an ARBITRARY python/ast
project -- including JanusMask itself -- by scanning a directory: classify each
``.py`` file as a rebuild target module, a pytest spec file, or seed scaffolding
(package ``__init__`` / ``conftest``), then synthesize the descriptor fields the
loop needs (full test command + per-unit ``-k`` selector).

Callers may still override any inferred field (``modules=`` / ``test_files=`` /
``seed_files=``) to rebuild a narrow SLICE of a large project without scanning
the whole tree (e.g. a single JanusMask leaf module into JR).
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import ast
from pathlib import Path
from harness.rebuild.deps import discover_dependencies
from harness.rebuild.target import TargetDescriptor
__all__ = ['discover_modules', 'build_descriptor', 'discover_dependencies', 'module_import_graph', 'order_modules', 'relative_base']
_SEED_NAMES = {'__init__.py', 'conftest.py'}
_SKIP_DIRS = {'__pycache__', '.git', '.hg', 'state', 'build', 'dist', '.eggs', 'node_modules'}

def _is_test_file(name: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if ``name`` is a pytest spec file basename.

    Test files are ``test_*.py`` or ``*_test.py``. Seed scaffolding such as
    ``conftest.py`` and package ``__init__.py`` is NOT a test file.
    """
    return name.endswith('.py') and (name.startswith('test_') or name.endswith('_test.py'))

def _skip_dir(rel_parts: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
    raise NotImplementedError

"""DISCOVER: build a TargetDescriptor from a BARE project directory.

Session #31's engine required a hand-authored descriptor (explicit module list,
test list, selector). This makes the engine work on an ARBITRARY python/ast
project -- including JanusMask itself -- by scanning a directory: classify each
``.py`` file as a rebuild target module, a pytest spec file, or seed scaffolding
(package ``__init__`` / ``conftest``), then synthesize the descriptor fields the
loop needs (full test command + per-unit ``-k`` selector).

Callers may still override any inferred field (``modules=`` / ``test_files=`` /
``seed_files=``) to rebuild a narrow SLICE of a large project without scanning
the whole tree (e.g. a single JanusMask leaf module into JR).

import ast
from pathlib import Path
from harness.rebuild.deps import discover_dependencies
from harness.rebuild.target import TargetDescriptor
__all__ = ['discover_modules', 'build_descriptor', 'discover_dependencies', 'module_import_graph', 'order_modules', 'relative_base']
_SEED_NAMES = {'__init__.py', 'conftest.py'}
_SKIP_DIRS = {'__pycache__', '.git', '.hg', 'state', 'build', 'dist', '.eggs', 'node_modules'}

def _is_test_file(name: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if ``name`` is a pytest spec file basename.

    Test files are ``test_*.py`` or ``*_test.py``. Seed scaffolding such as
    ``conftest.py`` and package ``__init__.py`` is NOT a test file.
    """
    return name.endswith('.py') and (name.startswith('test_') or name.endswith('_test.py'))

def _skip_dir(rel_parts: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
    """Return True if any path component marks a directory to skip while scanning.

    A directory is skipped when any of its relative path components is a hidden
    dir (leading ``.``, e.g. ``.git`` / ``.venv``) or a known non-source dir in
    ``_SKIP_DIRS`` (``__pycache__``, ``state``, build artifacts, ...). Ordinary
    source packages such as ``mypkg`` are not skipped.
    """
    return any((part in _SKIP_DIRS or part.startswith('.') for part in rel_parts))

def discover_modules(source_root: Path) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[str]]:
    """Scan ``source_root`` and return ``(modules, test_files, seed_files)``.

    Paths are returned relative to ``source_root``, POSIX-style, sorted. Test
    files (``test_*.py`` / ``*_test.py``) and seeds (``__init__.py`` /
    ``conftest.py``) are NOT rebuild targets; everything else is a module.
    Hidden dirs, ``__pycache__``, ``state``, and build artifacts are skipped.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def _stem_map(modules: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Map an import name -> module rel path for intra-project resolution.

    A flat module ``casing.py`` is importable as ``casing``; a packaged module
    ``pkg/sub.py`` as ``pkg.sub`` (and, best-effort, its leaf ``sub``). Both the
    dotted path and the leaf are registered so ``import casing`` and
    ``from pkg.sub import x`` both resolve.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

def relative_base(importing_rel: str, level: int) -> list[str] | None:
    """Return the absolute dotted prefix a relative import resolves against.

    For a module ``pkg/sub.py`` (dotted ``pkg.sub``, package ``pkg``) a
    ``level``-dot relative import drops ``level-1`` trailing components from the
    importing module's PACKAGE (Python's ``importlib`` semantics): ``level=1`` ->
    ``['pkg']`` (current package), ``level=2`` -> ``[]`` (parent / top-level).

    invalid relative import). Callers append the imported module/name to build the
    absolute dotted target, then resolve it via :func:`_stem_map`.
    """
    package_parts = importing_rel.split('/')[:-1]
    cut = len(package_parts) - (level - 1)

    return package_parts[:cut]

def _stem_map(modules: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Map an import name -> module rel path for intra-project resolution.

    A flat module ``casing.py`` is importable as ``casing``; a packaged module
    ``pkg/sub.py`` as ``pkg.sub`` (and, best-effort, its leaf ``sub``). Both the
    dotted path and the leaf are registered so ``import casing`` and
    ``from pkg.sub import x`` both resolve.
    """
    stem: dict[str, str] = {}
    for rel in modules:
        dotted = rel[:-3].replace("/", ".") if rel.endswith(".py") else rel.replace("/", ".")
        stem[dotted] = rel
        leaf = dotted.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
        stem.setdefault(leaf, rel)
    return stem

def relative_base(importing_rel: str, level: int) -> list[str] | None:
    """Return the absolute dotted prefix a relative import resolves against.

    For a module ``pkg/sub.py`` (dotted ``pkg.sub``, package ``pkg``) a
    ``level``-dot relative import drops ``level-1`` trailing components from the
    importing module's PACKAGE (Python's ``importlib`` semantics): ``level=1`` ->

def relative_base(importing_rel: str, level: int) -> list[str] | None:
    """Return the absolute dotted prefix a relative import resolves against.

    importing module's PACKAGE (Python's ``importlib`` semantics): ``level=1`` ->

    absolute dotted target, then resolve it via :func:`_stem_map`.

    if cut < 0:

    return package_parts[:cut]

    / ``from . import x`` are resolved through :func:`relative_base` to the
    absolute package, then each ``from . import <name>`` submodule (or the single
    ``from .x`` module) is returned. Empty when a relative import is out of bounds.

import ast

def relative_base(importing_rel: str, level: int) -> list[str] | None:

    Returns ``None`` when the level ascends beyond the top-level package (an

    absolute dotted target, then resolve it via :func:`_stem_map`.
    """
    package_parts = importing_rel.split('/')[:-1]
    cut = len(package_parts) - (level - 1)
    if cut < 0:

    return package_parts[:cut]


def _import_from_targets(importing_rel: str, node: ast.ImportFrom) -> list[str]:
    """Absolute dotted module name(s) an ``ImportFrom`` (absolute OR relative) names.

    Absolute ``from pkg.x import y`` -> ``['pkg.x']``. Relative ``from .x import y``
    / ``from . import x`` are resolved through :func:`relative_base` to the
    absolute package, then each ``from . import <name>`` submodule (or the single
    ``from .x`` module) is returned. Empty when a relative import is out of bounds.
    """
    if not node.level:

    base = relative_base(importing_rel, node.level)
    if base is None:
        return []
    if node.module:
        return ['.'.join(base + node.module.split('.'))]
    return ['.'.join(base + [alias.name]) for alias in node.names]


def _stem_map(modules: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Map an import name -> module rel path for intra-project resolution.

    dotted path and the leaf are registered so ``import casing`` and
    ``from pkg.sub import x`` both resolve.

    stem: dict[str, str] = {}

        dotted = rel[:-3].replace('/', '.') if rel.endswith('.py') else rel.replace('/', '.')

        leaf = dotted.rsplit('.', 1)[-1]
        stem.setdefault(leaf, rel)
    return stem

def relative_base(importing_rel: str, level: int) -> list[str] | None:
    """Return the absolute dotted prefix a relative import resolves against.

    For a module ``pkg/sub.py`` (dotted ``pkg.sub``, package ``pkg``) a
    ``level``-dot relative import drops ``level-1`` trailing components from the
    importing module's PACKAGE (Python's ``importlib`` semantics): ``level=1`` ->
    ``['pkg']`` (current package), ``level=2`` -> ``[]`` (parent / top-level).
    Returns ``None`` when the level ascends beyond the top-level package (an
    invalid relative import). Callers append the imported module/name to build the
    absolute dotted target, then resolve it via :func:`_stem_map`.
    """
    package_parts = importing_rel.split('/')[:-1]
    cut = len(package_parts) - (level - 1)
    if cut < 0:
        return None
    return package_parts[:cut]


def _import_from_targets(importing_rel: str, node: ast.ImportFrom) -> list[str]:
    """Absolute dotted module name(s) an ``ImportFrom`` (absolute OR relative) names.

    Absolute ``from pkg.x import y`` -> ``['pkg.x']``. Relative ``from .x import y``
    / ``from . import x`` are resolved through :func:`relative_base` to the
    absolute package, then each ``from . import <name>`` submodule (or the single
    ``from .x`` module) is returned. Empty when a relative import is out of bounds.

    if not node.level:
        return [node.module] if node.module else []
    base = relative_base(importing_rel, node.level)
    if base is None:
        return []
    if node.module:
        return ['.'.join(base + node.module.split('.'))]
    return ['.'.join(base + [alias.name]) for alias in node.names]

    ``pkg/sub.py`` as ``pkg.sub`` (and, best-effort, its leaf ``sub``). Both the
    dotted path and the leaf are registered so ``import casing`` and

    A directory is skipped when any of its relative path components is a hidden
    dir (leading ``.``, e.g. ``.git`` / ``.venv``) or a known non-source dir in
    ``_SKIP_DIRS`` (``__pycache__``, ``state``, build artifacts, ...). Ordinary
    source packages such as ``mypkg`` are not skipped.
    """
    return any((part in _SKIP_DIRS or part.startswith('.') for part in rel_parts))

def discover_modules(source_root: Path) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[str]]:
    """Scan ``source_root`` and return ``(modules, test_files, seed_files)``.

    Paths are returned relative to ``source_root``, POSIX-style, sorted. Test
    files (``test_*.py`` / ``*_test.py``) and seeds (``__init__.py`` /
    ``conftest.py``) are NOT rebuild targets; everything else is a module.
    Hidden dirs, ``__pycache__``, ``state``, and build artifacts are skipped.
    """
    modules: list[str] = []
    test_files: list[str] = []
    seed_files: list[str] = []
    for path in source_root.rglob('*.py'):
        rel = path.relative_to(source_root)
        if _skip_dir(rel.parts[:-1]):
            continue
        rel_posix = rel.as_posix()
        name = path.name
        if _is_test_file(name):
            test_files.append(rel_posix)
        elif name in _SEED_NAMES:
            seed_files.append(rel_posix)
        else:
            modules.append(rel_posix)
    return (sorted(modules), sorted(test_files), sorted(seed_files))

def _stem_map(modules: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Map an import name -> module rel path for intra-project resolution.

    A flat module ``casing.py`` is importable as ``casing``; a packaged module
    ``pkg/sub.py`` as ``pkg.sub`` (and, best-effort, its leaf ``sub``). Both the
    dotted path and the leaf are registered so ``import casing`` and
    ``from pkg.sub import x`` both resolve.
    """
    stem: dict[str, str] = {}
    for rel in modules:
        dotted = rel[:-3].replace('/', '.') if rel.endswith('.py') else rel.replace('/', '.')
        stem[dotted] = rel
        leaf = dotted.rsplit('.', 1)[-1]
        stem.setdefault(leaf, rel)
    return stem

def relative_base(importing_rel: str, level: int) -> list[str] | None:
    """Return the absolute dotted prefix a relative import resolves against.

    For a module ``pkg/sub.py`` (dotted ``pkg.sub``, package ``pkg``) a
    ``level``-dot relative import drops ``level-1`` trailing components from the
    importing module's PACKAGE (Python's ``importlib`` semantics): ``level=1`` ->
    ``['pkg']`` (current package), ``level=2`` -> ``[]`` (parent / top-level).
    Returns ``None`` when the level ascends beyond the top-level package (an
    invalid relative import). Callers append the imported module/name to build the
    absolute dotted target, then resolve it via :func:`_stem_map`.
    """
    package_parts = importing_rel.split('/')[:-1]
    cut = len(package_parts) - (level - 1)
    if cut < 0:
        return None
    return package_parts[:cut]

def _import_from_targets(importing_rel: str, node: ast.ImportFrom) -> list[str]:
    """Absolute dotted module name(s) an ``ImportFrom`` (absolute OR relative) names.

    Absolute ``from pkg.x import y`` -> ``['pkg.x']``. Relative ``from .x import y``
    / ``from . import x`` are resolved through :func:`relative_base` to the
    absolute package, then each ``from . import <name>`` submodule (or the single
    ``from .x`` module) is returned. Empty when a relative import is out of bounds.
    """
    if not node.level:
        return [node.module] if node.module else []
    base = relative_base(importing_rel, node.level)
    if base is None:
        return []
    if node.module:
        return ['.'.join(base + node.module.split('.'))]
    return ['.'.join(base + [alias.name]) for alias in node.names]

def module_import_graph(source_root: Path, modules: list[str]) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
    """Return ``{module_rel: set(intra-project module_rels it imports)}``.

    Only edges to OTHER modules in ``modules`` count (external deps and stdlib
    are ignored). Both top-level and function-local imports are considered, so a
    lazily-imported cross-module dependency still orders/taints correctly. A
    module never depends on itself.
    """
    stem = _stem_map(modules)
    graph: dict[str, set[str]] = {rel: set() for rel in modules}
    for rel in modules:
        try:
            source = (source_root / rel).read_text(encoding='utf-8')
            tree = ast.parse(source)
        except (OSError, SyntaxError, ValueError):
            continue
        targets: list[str] = []
        for node in ast.walk(tree):
            if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
                targets.extend((alias.name for alias in node.names))
            elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
                targets.extend(_import_from_targets(rel, node))
        for dotted in targets:
            dep = stem.get(dotted)
            if dep is not None and dep != rel:
                graph[rel].add(dep)
    return graph

def order_modules(source_root: Path, modules: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Order ``modules`` so an imported (callee) module precedes its importer.

    Deterministic depth-first topological order over
    :func:`module_import_graph`; ties and import CYCLES fall back to the given
    source order (so a circular ``a <-> b`` import pair is stable, never an
    error). Unit-level call dependencies are resolved separately by the loop, so
    a module-level cycle does not block reconstruction.
    """
    graph = module_import_graph(source_root, modules)
    ordered: list[str] = []
    done: set[str] = set()
    on_path: set[str] = set()

    def visit(rel: str) -> None:
        if rel in done:
            return
        on_path.add(rel)
        for dep in modules:
            if dep in graph[rel] and dep not in on_path:
                visit(dep)
        on_path.discard(rel)
        done.add(rel)
        ordered.append(rel)
    for rel in modules:
        visit(rel)
    return ordered

def build_descriptor(source_root: Path, *, output_dir: Path, stash_dir: Path, name: str | None=None, modules: list[str] | None=None, test_files: list[str] | None=None, seed_files: list[str] | None=None, dependencies: list[str] | None=None, requirements_files: list[str] | None=None) -> TargetDescriptor:

    ``requirements_files`` they came from are discovered via
    :func:`harness.rebuild.deps.discover_dependencies` unless supplied (so the
    replicant can provision its own ``.venv`` and run standalone).
    """

"""TargetDescriptor: declarative spec of a project the rebuild engine rebuilds.

A descriptor names the source modules to skeletonize, the test files that act
as the behavioral spec (copied verbatim), any seed/scaffolding files (package
``__init__``, conftest) the tests need to run in isolation, and where the
reconstructed replicant lands.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
from dataclasses import dataclass
from dataclasses import field
from pathlib import Path

@dataclass
class TargetDescriptor:
    """Everything the engine needs to rebuild a project clean-room.

    Attributes:
        name: Short slug used in task ids and commit messages.
        source_root: Absolute dir holding the original modules (read-only oracle).
        modules: Rel paths (under source_root) of .py modules to strip + rebuild.
        test_files: Rel paths of pytest files copied VERBATIM (the spec).
        output_dir: Absolute dir the skeleton + reconstructed code land in (its
            own git repo). MUST be distinct from source_root.
        stash_dir: Absolute dir (OUTSIDE output_dir) where original bodies are
            stashed for the oracle gate. Never committed into the replicant, so
            the replicant stays genuinely body-free until the agents fill it.
        seed_files: Rel paths copied VERBATIM into output_dir as scaffolding so
            the tests import-resolve in isolation (e.g. ``harness/__init__.py``).
        full_test_command: Whole-suite verification run in output_dir at VERIFY.
        unit_test_selector: pytest argument template scoping a single unit's
            tests; ``{unit}`` is substituted with the unit name. Empty -> the
            unit verification falls back to the bare test files.
        dependencies: External (3rd-party) pip-installable requirement lines the
            replicant needs to run -- discovered from requirements/pyproject/AST.
            Materialized into ``<out>/requirements.txt`` and installed into the
            replicant's own ``.venv`` so a clone runs standalone.
        requirements_files: Rel paths (under source_root) of the requirement
            manifests the deps were sourced from (audit trail).
        python_exe: Resolved interpreter the per-unit + full-suite verification
            run under -- the replicant's ``<out>/.venv/bin/python`` once
            provisioned, else ``None`` (ambient ``python``). The merged==original
            ORACLE always stays on the parent ambient python (it imports
            ``harness``); only the scoped pytest + full suite use this.
    """
    name: str
    source_root: Path
    modules: list[str]
    test_files: list[str]
    output_dir: Path
    stash_dir: Path
    seed_files: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    full_test_command: str = 'python -m pytest -q'
    unit_test_selector: str = ''
    dependencies: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    requirements_files: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    python_exe: str | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Normalize the path fields to absolute, resolved ``Path`` objects.

        Accepts ``str`` or ``Path`` for ``source_root``, ``output_dir`` and
        ``stash_dir``; each is coerced to a ``Path`` and ``.resolve()``d so the
        stored value is absolute and free of ``..`` segments. The remaining
        fields keep their declared values / defaults untouched.
        """
        self.source_root = Path(self.source_root).resolve()
        self.output_dir = Path(self.output_dir).resolve()
        self.stash_dir = Path(self.stash_dir).resolve()
    'Everything the engine needs to rebuild a project clean-room.'
from harness.rebuild.target import TargetDescriptor

def mathlib_descriptor(output_dir: Path, stash_dir: Path, source_root: Path) -> TargetDescriptor:
    """Build the descriptor for the shipped samples/mathlib smoke target."""
    return TargetDescriptor(name='mathlib', source_root=source_root, modules=['mathlib.py'], test_files=['test_mathlib.py'], output_dir=output_dir, stash_dir=stash_dir, seed_files=[], unit_test_selector='test_mathlib.py -k {unit}')

def janusmask_module_descriptor(name: str, modules: list[str], test_files: list[str], output_dir: Path, stash_dir: Path, source_root: Path, seed_files: list[str] | None=None, unit_test_selector: str='') -> TargetDescriptor:
    """Build a descriptor for rebuilding JanusMask's own leaf module(s) into JR."""
    full_test_command = 'python -m pytest -q ' + ' '.join(test_files)
    return TargetDescriptor(name=name, source_root=source_root, modules=modules, test_files=test_files, output_dir=output_dir, stash_dir=stash_dir, seed_files=list(seed_files) if seed_files is not None else [], full_test_command=full_test_command, unit_test_selector=unit_test_selector)
'TargetDescriptor: declarative spec of a project the rebuild engine rebuilds.'

1	"""DEPS: discover a project's EXTERNAL dependencies + the units that use them.
2	
3	The clean-room rebuild engine needs to reconstruct a project in an
4	environment-faithful way: a unit that imports a 3rd-party package can't be
5	rebuilt BLIND against the merged==original oracle (the dep is unavailable /
6	nondeterministic), so it must be routed to the oracle-skip + fuzzer-bypass
7	path. Two responsibilities live here:
8	
9	  * :func:`discover_dependencies` -- extract the project's declared external
10	    deps (and the manifest files they came from), trying requirements files,
11	    ``pyproject.toml``, ``setup.cfg``, ``setup.py`` in that order, with a
12	    last-resort AST import scan. The FIRST source that yields a dependency
13	    wins; sources are never merged.
14	  * :func:`external_units` -- given one module's source and the set of known
15	    external top-level package names, return the names of the functions /
16	    methods whose body references a name bound from one of those deps.
17	
18	Pure stdlib only (``ast`` / ``re`` / ``sys`` / ``configparser`` / ``tomllib``
19	/ ``pathlib``); no filesystem access outside ``source_root`` and no
20	home-directory lookups (clone-portable).
21	"""
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	import ast
24	import configparser
25	import re
26	import sys
27	import tomllib
28	from pathlib import Path
29	_SKIP_DIRS = {'__pycache__', '.git', '.hg', 'state', 'build', 'dist', '.eggs', 'node_modules', '.tox', '.venv', 'venv', '.mypy_cache', '.pytest_cache'}
30	
31	def _norm_name(dep: str) -> str:
32	    """PEP 503 normalized project name of a requirement string (or '').
33	
34	    Reads the leading name token (stopping at the first version operator,
35	    extras bracket, marker, or URL ``@``), then lowercases and collapses every
36	    run of ``-`` / ``_`` / ``.`` to a single ``-``.
37	    """
38	    match = re.match('\\s*([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)', dep)
39	    if not match:
40	        return ''
41	    return re.sub('[-_.]+', '-', match.group(1)).lower()
42	
43	def _dedup(deps: list[str]) -> list[str]:
44	    """De-duplicate by PEP 503 normalized name, preserving the first-seen line."""
45	    seen: set[str] = set()
46	    result: list[str] = []
47	    for dep in deps:
48	        name = _norm_name(dep)
49	        if not name or name in seen:
50	            continue
51	        seen.add(name)
52	        result.append(dep)
53	    return result
54	
55	def _include_target(line: str) -> str | None:
56	    """Return the FILE of a ``-r FILE`` / ``--requirement FILE`` line, else None."""
57	    match = re.match('\\s*(?:-r|--requirement)(?:\\s+|\\s*=\\s*)(.+)', line)
58	    if not match:
59	        return None
60	    return match.group(1).strip().strip('\'"') or None
61	
62	def _from_requirements(root: Path) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
63	    """Parse ``requirements*.txt`` / ``requirements.lock`` at ``root``.
64	
65	    Returns ``(deps, requirements_files)``. Comment lines and inline comments
66	    are stripped, blank lines dropped, ``-`` option lines skipped EXCEPT
67	    ``-r``/``--requirement`` includes (followed recursively, relative to
68	    ``root``). Each manifest actually read is recorded as a rel POSIX path.
69	    """
70	    deps: list[str] = []
71	    files: list[str] = []
72	    seen: set[Path] = set()
73	
74	    def _read(path: Path) -> None:
75	        resolved = path.resolve()
76	        if resolved in seen or not path.is_file():
77	            return
78	        seen.add(resolved)
79	        files.append(path.relative_to(root).as_posix())
80	        for raw in path.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').splitlines():
81	            line = raw.strip()
82	            if not line or line.startswith('#'):
83	                continue
84	            line = re.split('\\s+#', line, maxsplit=1)[0].strip()
85	            if not line:
86	                continue
87	            if line.startswith('-'):
88	                target = _include_target(line)
89	                if target is not None:
90	                    _read(root / target)
91	                continue
92	            deps.append(line)
93	    manifests = sorted(root.glob('requirements*.txt'))
94	    lock = root / 'requirements.lock'
95	    if lock.is_file():
96	        manifests.append(lock)
97	    for manifest in manifests:
98	        _read(manifest)
99	    return (deps, files)
100	
101	def _from_pyproject(root: Path) -> list[str]:
102	    """``[project].dependencies`` + ``[tool.poetry.dependencies]`` keys (no 'python')."""
103	    path = root / 'pyproject.toml'
104	    if not path.is_file():
105	        return []
106	    try:
107	        data = tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'))
108	    except (tomllib.TOMLDecodeError, OSError):
109	        return []
110	    deps: list[str] = []
111	    project = data.get('project')
112	    if isinstance(project, dict):
113	        for dep in project.get('dependencies') or []:
114	            if isinstance(dep, str):
115	                deps.append(dep)
116	    tool = data.get('tool')
117	    if isinstance(tool, dict):
118	        poetry = tool.get('poetry')
119	        if isinstance(poetry, dict):
120	            poetry_deps = poetry.get('dependencies')
121	            if isinstance(poetry_deps, dict):
122	                deps.extend((name for name in poetry_deps if name != 'python'))
123	    return deps
124	
125	def _from_setup_cfg(root: Path) -> list[str]:
126	    """``[options] install_requires`` (one dependency per line)."""
127	    path = root / 'setup.cfg'
128	    if not path.is_file():
129	        return []
130	    parser = configparser.ConfigParser()
131	    try:
132	        parser.read(path, encoding='utf-8')
133	    except (configparser.Error, OSError):
134	        return []
135	    raw = parser.get('options', 'install_requires', fallback='')
136	    deps: list[str] = []
137	    for line in raw.splitlines():
138	        dep = line.strip()
139	        if dep:
140	            deps.append(dep)
141	    return deps
142	
143	def _from_setup_py(root: Path) -> list[str]:
144	    """Best-effort: a literal ``install_requires=[...]`` string list (AST)."""
145	    path = root / 'setup.py'
146	    if not path.is_file():
147	        return []
148	    try:
149	        tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'))
150	    except (SyntaxError, ValueError, OSError):
151	        return []
152	    for node in ast.walk(tree):
153	        if isinstance(node, ast.keyword) and node.arg == 'install_requires' and isinstance(node.value, ast.List):
154	            deps: list[str] = []
155	            for elt in node.value.elts:
156	                if isinstance(elt, ast.Constant) and isinstance(elt.value, str):
157	                    deps.append(elt.value)
158	            return deps
159	    return []
160	
161	def _project_py_files(root: Path) -> list[Path]:
162	    """Rel paths of the project's own ``.py`` files (skipping vendor/build dirs)."""
163	    result: list[Path] = []
164	    for path in sorted(root.rglob('*.py')):
165	        rel = path.relative_to(root)
166	        if any((part in _SKIP_DIRS for part in rel.parts)):
167	            continue
168	        result.append(rel)
169	    return result
170	
171	def _intra_project_names(root: Path, py_files: list[Path]) -> set[str]:
172	    """Top-level package/module names owned by the project (+ ``source_root.name``)."""
173	    names: set[str] = {root.name}
174	    for rel in py_files:
175	        parts = rel.parts
176	        if not parts:
177	            continue
178	        if len(parts) == 1:
179	            names.add(rel.stem)
180	        else:
181	            names.add(parts[0])
182	    return names

184	def _from_ast(root: Path) -> list[str]:

186

189	    package/module names. Relative imports are intra-project and ignored.

214	    """Discover ``(dependencies, requirements_files)`` for ``source_root``.
215

217	    ``pyproject.toml``, ``setup.cfg``, ``setup.py``, then an AST import scan --
218	    and the FIRST that yields any dependency wins (sources are not merged).
219	    Dependencies are de-duplicated by PEP 503 normalized name (the first-seen
220	    line, with its version specifier, is kept). ``requirements_files`` always
221	    lists every requirements manifest found as a rel POSIX path, regardless of
222	    which source supplied the dependencies.
223	    """

225	    deps, requirements_files = _from_requirements(root)
226	    if not deps:

228	    if not deps:
229	        deps = _from_setup_cfg(root)
230	    if not deps:
231	        deps = _from_setup_py(root)

254	        ``_references`` helper, OR

256	        (e.g. ``def f(): import inflection`` or ``def f(): from inflection
